correctness.rationale: The one-dimensional deficit is computed in closed form and its second derivative has one sign change; together with endpoint values this makes the deficit strictly positive except at masses 0, 1/2, and 1. Splitting the last coordinate gives an exact nonnegative decomposition into the weighted lower-dimensional deficits, a Jensen--Shannon/mutual-information term, and the conditional one-dimensional deficit. Equality with both slices nonzero therefore forces equal slice masses, lower-dimensional equality, and identical Fourier moduli. For phased affine cubes the autocorrelation coefficients recover the signed generator directions from the largest nonzero magnitude and recover phase increments; thus equal Fourier magnitude forces translation plus a constant phase between classified slices. Induction gives exactly one additional independent Boolean generator, while the converse factorizes through the surjective torus homomorphism induced by integer-linearly independent generators. A fresh symbolic recomputation verified the one-dimensional derivative identity; finite numerical checks in the package are supplementary.
